siding_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net siding field area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. ~30 sec per LF. Includes staking and securing tarps at grade line. LF-based — measured along foundation/siding line. Identical rate to fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage adequate along working elevation. Minor gaps acceptable if no spray overspray risk.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter coverage of plantings within spray drift zone (10-15 ft). Secure against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete perimeter coverage secured at all edges. No gaps in protection.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on flat walkway and patio surfaces. ~14 sec per SF. Identical rate to fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways and patios within overspray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Fixture and Utility Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape light fixtures, utility panels, hose bibs. ~4 min per fixture. HVAC units take longer (~10 min). Identical rate to fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. All fixtures and utilities fully masked.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with clean tape lines. Cover plates removed where accessible.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer with 517 tip, 60-mesh filter, run lines, stage materials (~45 min). For spray_backroll: also stage roller frame + 18-inch covers (+5 min). Per elevation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern on cardboard. Correct tip for profile. Roller covers staged for spray_backroll.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified at correct distance. Backup tips staged. Fresh roller covers for back-rolling.

task_production_rates.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage brushes, rollers, trays, extension poles, and access equipment (~20 min). Per elevation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Fresh roller covers. Brushes in good condition.
defect_tolerance.QT4: New roller covers. Premium brushes. Materials pre-mixed.

task_production_rates.name: Low-Pressure Wash
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Garden hose + soft bristle brush. ~6 sec per SF. Same rate as fiber cement — both use low-pressure method. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING PROHIBITED on engineered wood — damages factory primer, forces water into OSB core at joints/cut edges.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All construction dust, dirt, and debris removed. Allow 24 hr dry time. Verify MC < 15%.
defect_tolerance.QT4: TSP solution wash. Pristine surface. Allow 24-48 hr dry time. Moisture meter check mandatory.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand for Adhesion
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 150-180 grit light scuff sand for adhesion profile. ~18 sec per SF. Required for factory-primed and factory-finished (ExpertFinish) surfaces. Not needed for bare wood or field-primed. Same rate as fiber cement scuff sand.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light scuff pattern visible. Not removing material — creating tooth.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform scratch pattern across full surface. No missed areas. Full surface scuff on ExpertFinish.

task_production_rates.name: End-Seal Field-Cut Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush LP SmartSide Cut End Seal on each field-cut edge. ~50 sec per cut edge. Includes butt joints, miters, and field cuts. MOST CRITICAL prep task — unsealed cut edges cause irreversible OSB core springback (FM-001). Same rate as fiber cement/wood siding end-seal.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Count of siding cut edges. Not captured by PaintScope — estimator enters count based on siding layout. Typical: 2-4 cuts per board for butt joints, window/door cutouts.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All cut edges sealed. Coverage adequate.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All cut edges sealed with full coverage. No bare OSB core visible at any cut.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All cut edges sealed. Inspect every joint, miter, and field cut for completeness. Critical for FM-001 prevention.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Siding-to-Trim Joints
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply and tool exterior paintable caulk at siding-to-trim joints. ~40 sec per LF. Do NOT caulk field butt joints — creates moisture trap against OSB core (per RF-012). Same rate as fiber cement caulk.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Linear feet of siding-to-trim joints requiring caulk. Includes corner board junctions, window/door casing junctions, frieze board junctions. Does NOT include field butt joints.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All siding-to-trim joints caulked. Smooth tool. No voids.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Uniform appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Content Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pin-type moisture meter checks at cut ends, joints, and low-elevation areas. ~3 sec per SF average. QT2 spot-checks only (faster). QT4 systematic with documentation (slower). Must read < 15% MC before coating. Engineered wood-specific task — more moisture-sensitive than fiber cement.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Spot check representative areas. Surface feels dry.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Check all cut ends, joints, and low-elevation areas. All readings < 15% MC.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic check with documented readings at all cut ends and joints. All areas < 15% MC.

task_production_rates.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Compressed air or tack cloth dust removal after sanding. ~6 sec per SF. Same rate as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All sanding dust removed. Surface ready for primer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Pristine surface. No visible dust. Tack cloth verification.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray primer on engineered wood siding. Factory-primed surface is sealed and less porous than bare wood — slightly faster than fiber cement primer (350 SF/hr) due to consistent factory-applied surface. ~9.6 sec per SF. Base rate for lap profile, smooth texture, ground access. Primer product driven by substrate state: acrylic (SYS_EXT_EW_PRIMER_ACRYLIC) for factory-primed/bare wood, bonding (SYS_EXT_EW_PRIMER_BONDING) for ExpertFinish.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Full coverage. Inspect for holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Spray + Back-Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Combined spray + immediate back-roll prime coat. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, roller follows while coating is wet. MANDATORY for T1-11 profile. Back-rolling distributes primer into vertical grooves and textured profiles. ~20.6 sec per SF combined. Base rate for lap profile — T1-11 is slower (apply FAC_ENSD_SIDING_PROFILE modifier). Rate per crew-hour (2 workers). Spray/backroll coupling: spray component rate (175 SF/hr) <= backroll component rate (175 SF/hr) — compliant.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Roller distributes primer into all grooves.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform distribution. No dry spots in channels. Roller follows sprayer within 30-60 seconds.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect groove coverage. Inspect all vertical channels at 3 ft. Consistent mil build across face and groove surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Brush/Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush for edges and transitions, roller for open field. ~36 sec per SF. Fallback method for <750 SF, occupied adjacent, or high wind. Same rate as fiber cement brush/roll prime.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Work primer into surface texture. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage with consistent roller texture. No lap marks.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat on primed engineered wood. Smooth LP SmartSide lap and panel profiles. ~10.3 sec per SF. Slightly faster than fiber cement spray (300 SF/hr) due to consistent factory-primed surface providing uniform absorption. No back-rolling for smooth profiles. Base rate for lap, smooth, ground access.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. No runs, sags, or curtaining.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray + Back-Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Combined spray + immediate back-roll finish coat. Two-person operation. MANDATORY for T1-11 — deep vertical grooves require roller distribution. Recommended for cedarmill and roughsawn textures. ~20.6 sec per SF combined. Rate per crew-hour (2 workers). Base rate for lap — T1-11 slower per FAC_ENSD_SIDING_PROFILE. Spray/backroll coupling: spray component (175) <= backroll component (175) — compliant.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Roller distributes paint into all grooves.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform distribution. No dry spots in T1-11 channels. Roller follows sprayer within 30-60 seconds.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect groove coverage. Inspect all vertical channels at 3 ft. Consistent mil build across face and groove.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush for edges, roller for field. Base rate for lap profile. ~36 sec per SF. Fallback method for <750 SF, occupied adjacent, or high wind. Same rate as fiber cement brush/roll.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Consistent roller texture. No brush marks on field. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No lap marks, roller marks, or brush marks visible at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Inspection

QT3.notes: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays. Check T1-11 grooves if applicable.

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Mark all visible defects. Raking light on visible elevations.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of first finish coat. QT3 quick scan, QT4 systematic with marking. For spray_backroll: also check T1-11 grooves for dry spots. Same rates as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Note obvious runs, sags, holidays. Quick visual scan.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic scan. All visible defects marked for repair. Raking light check on primary elevations.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Light Sand
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 220 grit light scuff between finish coats for adhesion and leveling. ~12 sec per SF. QT4 only — not required at QT3. Same rate as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light uniform scuff. Remove nibs and defects. No deep scratches. Do not sand through primer or first coat.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Touch-Up

QT4.notes: Fix all found defects. Blend repairs into surrounding finish.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during interstage inspection. QT3 minimal, QT4 thorough with blending. Same rates as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects repaired. No visible runs or holidays remain.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired and blended. Repairs invisible at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth or compressed air dust removal after interstage sanding. ~6 sec per SF. QT4 only (paired with TSK_ENSD_SAND_BETWEEN).

defect_tolerance.QT4: All sanding dust removed. Surface clean for second finish coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray. Primed and first-coated surface provides consistent absorption. Final appearance coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. No visible pattern at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray + Back-Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray_backroll. Consistent texture on T1-11 and textured profiles. Two-person operation. Final appearance coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even distribution in all grooves. Consistent appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect coverage. Every groove filled. Inspect at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 brush/roll. Final coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. No brush marks. Maintain wet edge. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No defects visible at 3 ft. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection

QT2.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses.

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check all elevations.

QT4.notes: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light on primary elevations.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final walkthrough of all elevations. For spray_backroll: also verify uniform groove coverage on T1-11. Same rates as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses or holidays visible from ground.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible at 6-10 ft from ground level.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 6 ft with binoculars. Coverage uniform across all elevations.

task_production_rates.name: Final Touch-Up

QT2.notes: Minimal touch-up. Fix obvious misses only.

QT4.notes: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft standard.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Same rates as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects repaired.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended seamlessly.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all tarps, plastic, tape, fixture bags, HVAC covers along perimeter. ~18 sec per LF. Faster than setup — pull and fold vs. stake and secure. Same rate as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials removed. No tape residue on surfaces. Check landscape for overspray.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All materials removed. Check for tape residue. Inspect for any paint on protected surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Flush airless sprayer, clean tips and filters, coil hoses. Clean brushes and rollers if used. For spray_backroll: also clean roller frames, dispose of saturated roller covers (+5 min vs fiber cement's 30 min). ~35 min per session.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full flush. Tips and filters cleaned. Roller covers disposed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full flush cycle. Tips and filters cleaned and inspected. Equipment ready for next use.

task_production_rates.name: Site Debris Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect debris (sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, sealer containers, paint cans, used roller covers), dispose, final site walkthrough. ~20 min. Same as fiber cement sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Site restored. Walkthrough with customer. No evidence of work activity.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Height Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type drives production rate reduction for elevated work. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior. Applied per elevation.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Ground tasks (end-seal, equipment setup, dust cleanup, site cleanup) are not affected — done at ground level or on sawhorses.

factor_modifiers.name: Siding Profile Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Siding profile dramatically affects application and prep rates. T1-11 is slowest due to mandatory back-rolling into vertical grooves and constant repositioning. Panel slightly slower than lap due to large flat areas requiring careful overlap management.
factor_modifiers.notes: Lap is baseline (long horizontal runs, fastest production). Panel slightly slower (fewer joints but large single runs require careful overlap). T1-11 dramatically slower — deep vertical grooves require roller distribution of coating at every groove. T1-11 1.80x: spray 350/1.80 = 194 SF/hr, spray_backroll 175/1.80 = 97 SF/hr. Research supports 150-200 SF/hr range for spray_backroll on T1-11.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Texture Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Textured profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn) require additional spray passes for DFT and slower production. Applies to both production rate and material quantity.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applies to BOTH production rate and material quantity (see coverage_profiles in materials.json). Textured profiles trap more paint in valleys, requiring additional passes for correct DFT. Same values as fiber cement surface texture modifier — texture geometry determines consumption, not substrate material.

quality_effects.notes: Economy tier. Single finish coat on primed surface. No interstage module. Minimal inspection. LP warranty requires minimum 2 coats but QT2 accepts the trade-off.
Standard tier. Two finish coats per LP SmartSide warranty. Interstage inspection but no sanding. Full edge seal and moisture check.
Premium tier. Two finish coats. Light 220 grit sand between coats. Systematic inspection at 6 ft. Premium LP-approved materials.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Lap siding, smooth, ground access — baseline (spray)
T1-11 siding, smooth, ground access — spray_backroll baseline
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: T1-11 at ground level. ~97 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Aligns with research range of 150-200 SF/hr for spray_backroll T1-11 (research rates are per single-worker, this is per crew-hour with 2 workers).

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Lap siding, cedarmill, ladder access — common residential (spray)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Typical residential scenario. ~216 SF/hr spray — reasonable production.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: T1-11 siding, roughsawn, scaffold access — worst case (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Near worst case — under 4.0x stacking cap. ~47 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Very slow but still fixed-price viable.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Panel siding, roughsawn, scaffold — upper bound check (spray)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Panel + roughsawn + scaffold. ~153 SF/hr spray — comfortable within 4.0x cap.

assumptions: Base rates are for lap siding profile at ground access on smooth surface.
Profile, texture, and access modifiers stack multiplicatively: effective_rate = base_rate / (profile x texture x access).
Modifier stacking cap: 4.0x maximum combined. No combination in this spec exceeds 4.0x (worst case T1-11 + roughsawn + scaffold = 3.744x).
spray_backroll tasks are single combined tasks (not separate spray and backroll tasks like wood siding) because SOP defines them as one operation. crew_size = 2 for spray_backroll tasks.
Spray/backroll coupling rule is satisfied: spray component rate (175 SF/hr) <= backroll component rate (175 SF/hr) within combined task.
Engineered wood spray rates (350 SF/hr finish, 375 SF/hr primer) are slightly faster than fiber cement (300, 350) due to more consistent factory-primed surface.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, surface temp) are NOT estimation modifiers per RC-003 — SOP reference only.
Edge seal and caulk rates assume ground-level work or sawhorses — not affected by FAC_EXT_ACCESS.
Moisture check is unique to this spec — engineered wood is more moisture-sensitive than fiber cement.
Equipment cleanup slightly longer than fiber cement (+5 min) due to roller cleaning for spray_backroll.
risks: T1-11 + roughsawn + scaffold is near the 4.0x stacking cap (3.744x) — flag for estimator review on these combinations.
spray_backroll 2-person crew requirement doubles labor cost on prime and finish application tasks.
End-seal count is manual capture — estimator must count cut edges from siding layout. Under-count risks OSB core springback.
Moisture check rates are estimate only — no field calibration data. Actual time depends on how many readings fail and require re-checking.
Back-roll roller consumption rate (1 EA per 500 SF) is assumption — flag for field calibration.
Factory-finished (ExpertFinish) substrate requires bonding primer — estimator must verify substrate state before pricing.
validation_plan: Time 3 spray finish projects on smooth lap engineered wood at ground access to calibrate baseline 350 SF/hr.
Time 2 spray_backroll projects on T1-11 to validate 175 SF/hr combined rate with 2-person crew.
Compare engineered wood spray rates vs fiber cement spray rates — expect EW to be 10-15% faster on smooth profiles.
Time cedarmill vs smooth production on same project to validate 1.20x texture modifier.
Track moisture check time per project to calibrate 1200 SF/hr baseline.
Track end-seal counts per project to develop estimating heuristic (cut edges per 100 SF of siding).
Compare equipment cleanup time: spray-only vs spray_backroll to validate 30 vs 35 min.
